name: Remote viewing (Octopus ring, CCW chirp 10->20 ms)
origin: Todd Murphy (his description of the psi signal and timing of Persinger's circumcerebral 'Octopus' and his Shiva replica); ring placement after the Persinger-lab Octopus
summary: Murphy's psi configuration for the circumcerebral Shiva/Octopus: the chirp signal, which he chose for psi, rotating counter-clockwise around an eight-coil ring with the time over each coil growing 10, 12 ... 20 ms and then starting again (about 8 turns a second), for 30 min. It is not the session Persinger's lab gave Ingo Swann; follow it with a blinded trial in the Experiment tab.
notes: Murphy's lecture gives the steps as 10, 12, 14, 16, 18 and 20 ms "with the length of time over each area increasing", and the Shiva pages say the speed changes by a few milliseconds from one coil pair to the next, "usually around 9 times per second"; here the dwell grows by 2 ms at every coil (one turn about 0.11-0.12 s). No Shiva dwell table is published, so the exact steps are an inference. The ring Fpz, F7, T7, P7, Oz, P8, T8, F8 approximates the lab Octopus, eight solenoids in the plane between the mid-forehead and above the ears, stepping counter-clockwise seen from above (front to back on the left, back to front on the right). Murphy's Shiva instead starts over the left frontal area and avoids coils over the nose, the inion and directly above the ears (about Fp1, FT7, TP7, O1, O2, TP8, FT8, Fp2; the site names are an inference); to copy it, use a custom placement with those sites in that order. The Shiva "modulated 40 Hz chirp" is proprietary, and Murphy describes it two ways: his lab-sessions page says it "does not change in tone, but rather has longer and longer gaps between sections of the signal as they travel around your head", while his chirp page shows a classical chirp whose frequency gets lower. It is approximated by a sweep falling from 40 to 6 Hz on 3-ms points, 2.5 s on and 1.5 s off. Murphy advises using the chirp on its own only after other Shiva sessions. 30 min is one of the Shiva session lengths (20, 30 or 60 min). Corrected: Persinger's lab gave Swann (Persinger et al. 2002, Table 1, read from a scan) one 30-min session of six 5-min configurations, three burst-firing and three frequency-modulated (Thomas), rotated counter-clockwise at 2-5 uT, with 20, 100 and 200 ms on the first coil and changes of +2, +20 and -2 ms per coil (signs as printed; their direction is ambiguous), 1- or 3-ms points and 1-ms or 3-s gaps between repeats; the remote-viewing trials came on later days. persinger-swann-2002-table1 runs that table. Murphy writes that Swann's clear remote viewing came during the final phase. Swann's accuracy correlated with occipital 7-Hz spike-and-slow-wave activity (rho = .50; one subject, no sham), and the paper does not test whether the fields changed accuracy; Murphy places psi in right-hemisphere hippocampal theta. The Octopus psi results have no independent replication, and independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Don't use results for decisions about real people, places or money. Not for people with epilepsy; stop on distress.
setting: Blindfolded, seated or reclined in a quiet room; Murphy says daydreaming is better than meditating during Shiva sessions. For perception during the session he advises geomagnetic quiet (K 0-2); for skill training, run it at K 4 and practise a few days later. Swann's later trials used 4-6 hidden targets per session with about 2-3 min of drawing each.
schedule: At most weekly (Murphy's rule for Shiva sessions); six sessions, then a 21-day break.
